messages:
julie_csm: FYI — TeleMed (EU) is seeing sudden 200–400ms extra tail latency and intermittent 401s since 03:20 UTC. Their traces show traffic landing in us-west1 instead of EU. They suspect DNS/GeoIP mismatch. Repro + logs below.

alex_dev: can you paste the resolver IP and one failing request id so we can trace?

julie_csm: resolver 203.0.113.58, failing request id req_01H3Z9X2, sample curl attached:

```
> curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/2 401
content-type: application/json
...
x-rw-pop: us-west1

{"error":"unauthorized"}
```

Also they ran dig from their resolver, output: 
```
$ dig @203.0.113.58 api.redwood.example A +edns +short
34.120.12.45
```
(we expected an EU IP 18.194.x.x)

sandeep_sre: that looks like EDNS client-subnet (ECS) being stripped by the resolver/ISP — common cause for anycast landing at a far POP. Do we log upstream LB chosen pop for these req_01H ids?

alex_dev: pulled proxy logs for req_01H3Z9X2 -> loadbalancer.log:
```
2026-10-12T03:20:14Z req=req_01H3Z9X2 src=203.0.113.58 pop=us-west1 route=primary status=401
```

sandeep_sre: confirms. Can the customer try a different public resolver (1.1.1.1 or 9.9.9.9) to confirm? If it fixes, it's definitely resolver-side.

julie_csm: they tested switching to 1.1.1.1 — latency dropped to ~30ms and 401s stopped. So that's a repro. They can't force all users to switch resolvers.

maya_net: opened ticket with our DNS provider FastDNS (FD-8342). FastDNS says their anycast advertised routes to that ASN don't preserve ECS for that upstream — the ASN's edge is rewriting/stripping EDNS. FastDNS recommends: lower DNS TTL temporarily and/or support a region-hint query param on our endpoints as short term. Long term: work with upstream peers to preserve ECS or build resolver-based affinity.

sandeep_sre: immediate mitigations we can do from platform side: 
- lower authoritative TTL for api.redwood.example from 300 -> 60 for the next 24h to reduce cache stickiness
- add a smart-routing fallback: if src ASN geolocation = EU but request landed at non-EU pop, prefer routing to EU pop (preserve auth semantics)
- log detailed impacted ASNs and TTL windows so we can roll back

alex_dev: quick patch idea: accept optional header x-rw-region from client to force region preference (document as best-effort). Customer could set it in their SDK as a stopgap. Example:
```
curl -H "x-rw-region: eu-west-1" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
This won't fix plain browser requests but helpful for server-to-server.

julie_csm: TeleMed confirmed they can set the header for their backend calls. They still have end-user devices on problematic ISPs though.

maya_net: fastdns responded — they will patch peering routes but estimate 24–48h. I also asked them to confirm whether they can enable ECS preservation selectively for that ASN.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: route-fallback-rule (canary) -> staging 2026-10-12T04:05Z, prod 2026-10-12T04:20Z (owner: sandeep_sre).

sandeep_sre: I'll push the TTL change now and roll the fallback rule as a canary. Will monitor 5xx/401 rates closely.

julie_csm: I've told TeleMed the mitigation plan: 1) have backend switch to x-rw-region header (works now), 2) we'll lower TTL + canary fallback, 3) FastDNS peering fix in 24–48h. Keeping them updated. :white_check_mark:

alex_dev: minor note — routing fallback must preserve token validation path (we revalidate with auth service in target region) to avoid increased 401s. I'll add extra auth proxy check in the canary.

sandeep_sre: agreed, added. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/d/route-ops/geoip-routing?from=now-15m

julie_csm: customer reported initial improvement after header + TTL change this morning. I'll close after FastDNS confirms peering change. Thanks everyone.
